title: Strict scalar cone augmentation and invariance
statement: On the module sheaf category of R, let H be a cochain functor and ρ:Id→H a natural transformation annihilating multiplication by t. There is a natural map C_t→H whose degree n component is the unshifted projection followed by ρ, and its composite with inclusion is ρ. For a coefficient adjunction E⊣Res along φ, if multiplication by t followed by R→Res S is zero, the termwise unit annihilates t. Scalar cone formation preserves every quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 06YP, 06YS, 06YY and Modules on Sites, Tag 03EK; normalized principal quotient construction.

proof.text: Use mappingCone.desc with zero shifted component and unshifted component ρ. The annihilation identity is its chain equation; the projection formulas give naturality and inclusion. Evaluate the coefficient-ring zero composite at 1 to get φ(t)=0. Thus the scalar is zero on every restricted module, and naturality makes its composite with the adjunction unit zero. For invariance, send the natural square on the scalar maps to a morphism of distinguished mapping-cone triangles in a standard derived category. The first two components are isomorphisms, so the third is too; localization reflects quasi-isomorphisms.
